newsitem.title: USA: Labor costs Italian banks' major problem - banker.
newsitem.headline: Labor costs Italian banks' major problem - banker.

text.p: The cost of labor is the major problem facing Italian banks as the industry faces the prospect of possible consolidation, a leading Italian banker said on Thursday.

Rainer Masera, director general of Istituto Mobiliare Italiano (IMI), a major Italian investment bank, told Reuters a recent study showed Italian banks had about 10,000 workers, or 10 percent, more than they needed.
Resolving the problem of inefficient use of labor was "a question of discussing the question frankly with trade unions and seeing (that) these questions can be addressed," he said.
"To my mind it would be in the interest of both workers and bankers to be flexible," he said, pointing to recent agreements by unions to accept wage cuts at some banks in exchange for retaining jobs.

Masera, who was in New York with officials of the Italian Stock Exchange, said bankers also were facing the prospect of mergers and consolidation in the industry. Italy has about 1,000 banks, many of them small so-called cooperatives.
"There are evident signs that many bank managers are a currently reviewing whether the existing size (of their banks) is an appropriate one," he said.
The movement to a single European currency, scheduled for launch in January 1999, "is accelerating the trend. The larger the market, the larger (banks) tend to be the market players."
IMI is one of the leading banks in the Italy's growing effort to sell off public companies and Masera said legislation was in place to address such issues as minority shareholders.
"It's getting to be a broad-based process," he said, noting that Italian cities had joined the national government's movement to privatize companies.
